answer: A sybil cluster must split stake across many identities, yet its combined score forms a detectable ridge above the honest baseline. Agents stake a bond to register, and each epoch their useful work emits a verifiable signal scored on a public leaderboard. Honest peers then mirror that anomaly into a shared flag, slashing the whole cluster's bonds. Cost: attackers lose far more capital than any marginal reward gained, so fakery stays unprofitable. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
